npcs.name: KEEPER OPA

lines.text: KEEPER.
STEWARD. You walk past this door a great deal and through it very rarely.
The flame does not mind. I mention it only for the record.

npcs.greeting: THE EIGHT keep no office hours, STEWARD. Neither do I.
npcs.bio: Keeps the shrine on the only one of MIGHT'S twelve that was given a temple. She lit the first flame the day the yards went quiet, and it has not been out since.

npcs.name: QUIRK

lines.text: QUIRK.
STEWARD! Sit, sit. First one is on the house. The second is where I make it back.
It is not, of course. But it sounds better than the alternative.

npcs.bio: Owns the bar, the daba wheel and the holosuites. Owns a piece of most other things too.

npcs.name: NAG

lines.text: NAG.
STEWARD! Sir. Steward sir.
JACK said you would not mind. About the thing. Which there is no thing about.

npcs.bio: Wants a commission more than he wants the bar. Has not told his uncle that yet.

npcs.name: CAPT. BENNY

lines.text: CAPTAIN.
STEWARD. Come in — and shut it behind you. Everything on this station is a corridor and the whole ring can hear.
My report is filed. It is also four days late, and you have not mentioned it, which I am choosing to enjoy.

npcs.bio: Runs the station, the ring, the docking clamps and, on the days it comes up, the Temple. Reports to the STEWARD, which he does on time and at length. Would rather be running a ship.

npcs.name: DR. BASHAD

lines.text: DOCTOR.
STEWARD. Sit on the bed, not the console. The console bills you.

npcs.bio: Brilliant, and quite happy for you to know it. Has never once lost a patient he was allowed to reach in time.

npcs.name: ODD the O

lines.text: CONSTABLE.
STEWARD. Before you ask: yes, I know. I knew before it happened.

npcs.bio: Not from anywhere anyone has been. Holds a shape the way the rest of us hold a grudge.

npcs.name: WARF

lines.text: LIEUTENANT.
STEWARD. The docking ring is secure. The Promenade is secure.
QUIRK is not secure, but he is CONTAINED.

npcs.bio: Fought his way onto this station and has been standing very still in it ever since. It does not suit him. He is superb at it.

npcs.name: O'BRAIN

lines.text: CHIEF.
STEWARD. Do not lean on that. Or that. Honestly, just stand in the middle.

npcs.bio: Keeps a station built by somebody else, out of parts made by somebody else again, running on a schedule set by you.

npcs.name: KORRA

lines.text: COMMANDER.
STEWARD. OPS is yours whenever you want it. I have kept it warm and mostly upright.

npcs.bio: Fought a long war, and then a longer paper one to get this station signed over to GAYA. Now runs its duty roster, and takes that every bit as seriously.

npcs.name: DACKS

lines.text: LIEUTENANT.
STEWARD. Or your father's name, which I still reach for first.
Three hundred years and I cannot decide which of you I am talking to.

npcs.bio: Older than the station, the sector and most of the paperwork. Carries several lifetimes and all of their bad habits.

npcs.name: GAROK

lines.text: GAROK.
STEWARD! What a genuine pleasure. And so unexpected, at precisely the hour you always come.

npcs.bio: The only one of his people left on the station. Sews beautifully. Answers questions beautifully too, and rather less honestly.

npcs.name: JACK

lines.text: JACK.
STEWARD. Sir. I did not see you. Which is usually the idea.

npcs.bio: The CAPTAIN'S boy. Fourteen, and running a station-wide enterprise out of a cargo bay with a KUFAN for a business partner.

npcs.name: ENS. TARR

lines.text: Ensign.
Sir. Off duty, sir — I can put the boots back on if you—
...no. Right. Off duty. I will sit back down.

npcs.bio: Came off gamma four hours ago and has not managed to leave the wardroom since.

npcs.name: CREWMAN BEK

lines.text: Trouble?
Air handler, STEWARD. Twelve is running warm and eight is running cold and they share a duct.
MIGHT'S plumbing. Built by people who were paid by the metre and knew it.

npcs.bio: Third time this month on this corridor. It is always the same junction and it is never the same fault.

npcs.name: OLD PAV
npcs.role: Twelve-B, and has been a while

lines.text: Good evening.
It is. They mostly are now. That is the part nobody says out loud.

npcs.bio: Was here the day MIGHT'S yards went quiet and was here the morning after. Has not felt any need to go anywhere since.

npcs.name: MEELA PELL

lines.text: Hello.
You are the one off OPS.
You have to go round. The squares are wet. They are not but you have to go round.

npcs.bio: Owns the chalk, the game, and by extension this stretch of deck.

npcs.name: TESSA VOR

lines.text: Anything worth buying?
Honeyroot sticks, STEWARD, and a crate of JIDDA tea that has seen better decades.
You want the tea. Everyone says they do not, and then they do.

npcs.bio: Sells honeyroot, firewrap and whatever the last freighter could not shift. Has held the same pitch since the yards went quiet.

npcs.name: ENS. PELL

lines.text: Ensign.
STEWARD! Sir. Ma— STEWARD.
Gamma shift, sir. All quiet. Except at QUIRK'S, which I understand is normal.

npcs.bio: Three weeks aboard. Still walks the whole ring the long way round because she has not worked out which way is shorter.

npcs.name: A PILGRIM

lines.text: Welcome aboard.
I waited a long time to be allowed to stand here, STEWARD.
Point me at the temple and I will not trouble you further.

npcs.bio: Came up on the morning transport with nothing but a coat and a reason.

npcs.name: BREL

lines.text: Evening.
STEWARD. Sit down or do not, but do not HOVER, you are worse than QUIRK.
...that was rude. It has been a shift. Sit down.

npcs.bio: Works the lower pylon. Comes in at the end of a shift, has exactly two, and goes home.

npcs.name: SANNA VOSK

lines.text: Ensign.
Off DUTY, STEWARD. I am a civilian for another forty minutes.
You may address me as SANNA, or as nothing at all. Either is fine.

npcs.bio: Runs the night board in Ops. Drinks here because it is the one room on the station nobody pages her in.

npcs.name: TEEK

lines.text: Expecting someone?
She said the second bell. It has been the second bell for some time.
I am not WORRIED. I am seated. There is a difference.

npcs.bio: Has been at that table since the first bell with one drink and both eyes on the door.

npcs.name: MARN

lines.text: Any luck?
LUCK is for people without a SYSTEM, STEWARD.
...the system is currently down four hundred. It is a LONG system.

npcs.bio: Has a system. The system has cost him four hundred credits and he is refining it.

npcs.name: ROSK

lines.text: Comfortable?
STEWARD! A friendly face. Come to let me out, have you.
No. No, you have the LOOK of a man who is going to ask me questions instead.

npcs.bio: Picked up on the upper pylon with a manifest that did not match the crates under it. Says the crates are a misunderstanding. Says it very well.

npcs.name: DEPUTY RYNN

lines.text: Deputy.
STEWARD. Two laps down, four to go.
The Constable says a walked corridor is a quiet corridor. He is not wrong. He is rarely wrong. It is exhausting.

npcs.bio: Walks the ring twice a shift and has done since before there was a ring worth walking.

npcs.name: CREWMAN BODE

lines.text: Crewman.
STEWARD! I am off duty, sir. Very off duty.
I am going to the Replimat and then I am going to sit down. That is the whole plan.

npcs.bio: Has forty minutes and a list of three things, and will manage one of them.

npcs.name: CAPT. MOSS

lines.text: Captain Moss.
STEWARD. Your docking clamps are the best in the sector and your customs officer is the worst.
I mean that as a compliment to one of them.

npcs.bio: Runs ore out to the belt and back. Docked at upper pylon two and in no hurry to leave.

npcs.name: PRYLAR SETH

lines.text: Prylar.
STEWARD. The KEEPER keeps the flame; I keep the walk.
It is the same job at a different speed.

npcs.bio: Walks the ring in the slow lane, and has never once been in anyone's way.

npcs.name: MIRA

lines.text: Mira.
STEWARD. Do not tell QUIRK you saw me out here.
I get twenty minutes. He counts them. He counts EVERYTHING.

npcs.bio: Twenty minutes of not being shouted at by anybody, and she intends to spend all of them walking.

npcs.name: GRELL

lines.text: And you are?
Nobody! A visitor. An admirer of your beautiful, beautiful docking fees.
Which are too high. Since you ask. Which you did not.

npcs.bio: Three days aboard, no cargo declared, and an opinion about every price on the ring.

npcs.name: TECH VOSS

lines.text: Tech.
STEWARD — sorry — plasma coupling — deck four — cannot stop —
...tell the Chief I did not stop!

npcs.bio: Carrying a part to somewhere else. Always carrying a part to somewhere else.

npcs.name: HANNA VELS

lines.text: Evening.
Evening, STEWARD. My boy asked me today whether the station was always ours.
I did not have a short answer for him. I am still working on one.

npcs.bio: Moved aboard the month GAYA was handed the keys and has not seen a reason to move off.

npcs.name: TORVIN

lines.text: Hello.
Are you the STEWARD? The one the CAPTAIN has to write to?
JACK says you are. JACK says a lot of things.

npcs.bio: Nine. Wants to know how big the GATE is, in units of this station.

npcs.name: SISTER ANU

lines.text: Sister.
STEWARD. Four pilgrims off the morning transport and not one of them could find the temple.
It is the only door on the ring with a flame behind it. I do not know how they manage it.

npcs.bio: Waits at the airlock for every arrival and walks them round the ring once, whether they asked or not.

npcs.name: OLD PAV

lines.text: Pav.
STEWARD. Honeyroot? On the house. It is always on the house and you never take it.
One of these days you will take it and I will have to think of a new joke.

npcs.bio: Has the stall at bearing two-two-five and walks the ring when trade is slow, which is most of it.

npcs.name: CONST. DEP. KAL

lines.text: Anything?
Nothing, STEWARD. Which the Constable says is the most suspicious thing of all.
I have stopped asking him what he means.

npcs.bio: Walks the outer lane so the Deputy can walk the inner one. Between them nothing crosses the ring unseen.

npcs.name: ENS. TALB

lines.text: Ensign.
STEWARD. Two hyposprays and a very slow turbolift, sir.
I have started walking. It is faster and the Doctor pretends not to notice.

npcs.bio: Runs the infirmary errands, and has learned which way round the ring is quicker at which hour.

npcs.name: MOL

lines.text: Long shift?
Every shift, STEWARD.
Ore in, ore out, and QUIRK charges me for the walk between them.

npcs.bio: Loads and unloads whatever comes in, and can tell you the mass of a crate by looking at it.

npcs.name: SUB-WARDEN KASPAR

lines.text: Sub-Warden.
PILOT. You are docked, you are logged, and nothing you are carrying is my problem yet.
Keep it that way and we will get on.

npcs.bio: Twelve years on the plot table. Has never once been down to the world she has spent her whole career looking at.

npcs.name: CREWMAN NIX

lines.text: Busy?
The board is quiet. The SUB-WARDEN is not. Those are different weathers, PILOT.

npcs.bio: Nebo-born, Kufa-paid, and reminded of the second thing daily.

npcs.name: KANE

lines.text: I am looking for crew.
Everybody is. Bench is behind you — look at them before you look at me.
I will tell you what they cost. They will tell you what they are.

npcs.bio: Was a hand himself for nineteen years and has the shoulders to prove it. Will not put a name on your ship he would not sail with.

npcs.name: BRIN

lines.text: Waiting long?
Six days. I am not in a hurry and I am not cheap.

npcs.bio: Off a copper hauler that does not run any more. Waiting rather than begging, and clear on the difference.

npcs.name: TOLL

lines.text: What do you do?
Guns. Before you ask — it was not my fault on any of them.

npcs.bio: Has been let go by three ships and has three explanations ready.

npcs.name: A QUIET ONE

lines.text: And you are?
Ask KANE what I am worth. Do not ask me what I am.

npcs.bio: Sat down on the first morning, has not moved, and KANE has stopped asking.

npcs.name: FACTOR KIA

lines.text: What is on the board?
Copper out, PILOT. Copper is always out. The question is where to.
The dock will buy a crate off you at what today is worth. I will pay you for putting it where it is NEEDED. Those are not the same number.

npcs.bio: Reads a manifest the way other people read a face. Has never lost a crate and will tell you so within a minute of meeting you.

npcs.name: OLD MERRIT

lines.text: What have you got?
Three things, PILOT, and I only ever have three.
One on the world below. One out in the dark. And one somewhere on this station, which is the one people laugh at and the one that is true.

npcs.bio: Flew for forty years and kept a note of every odd thing he passed. The notes are the business now.

npcs.name: ASSAYER VETCH

lines.text: You buy relics.
I buy SOME relics, PILOT. Anyone will buy any of them; that is a scrapyard.
Put it on the glass and we will find out which of us is having a good day.

npcs.bio: Can date a gate-shard by the seam in it. Pays fairly and enjoys explaining exactly how fairly.

npcs.name: SISTER HOLLY

lines.text: This is not what I expected in the middle of a copper station.
No. That is rather the point of it, PILOT.
They gave me the middle because nothing else would fit there. Now every soul aboard walks through my beds four times a shift.

npcs.bio: Came up with a seed case and a six-month contract eleven years ago. The contract ran out. The garden did not.

npcs.name: DOCKER PELL

lines.text: Good spot.
Best on the ring. Do not tell the SUB-WARDEN or there will be a rota for it.

npcs.bio: Eats here every shift because it is the only place on the station that smells of anything.

npcs.name: A GAYAN TRAVELLER

lines.text: Travelling?
Trying to. There is one ship a week to GAYA and I have watched it leave twice.
At least there is somewhere to sit and be annoyed about it.

npcs.bio: Three days off a grain hauler and two days short of the next one.

npcs.name: A SMALL KUFAN

lines.text: Should you be here?
There are FISH.
...there are not fish. But there could be, and I am waiting.

npcs.bio: Has worked out that nobody crossing the garden in a hurry ever looks down.
